issues.failure_explanation: The objective attains its minimum 0 at every root of p(ξ)^m = e^{λmh}, i.e., at p(ξ) = e^{λh}ω for any m-th root of unity ω, so for m > 1 there are extra global minimizers beyond the root satisfying p(ξ) = e^{λh}. These violate the corollaries' conclusions: for Forward Euler with m = 2 and λh = iπ/2, both ξ = −1±i give zero loss, and ξ = −1−i has Im(λ̂h) < 0 while Im(λ) > 0 (violating thm:fe_cons's sign claim); with m = 4, ξ = 0 is a zero-loss minimizer with Re(λ̂h) = 0, violating Re(λ̂) < 0. Even for m = 1 the Runge–Kutta corollaries have several global minimizers (all roots of p(ξ) = e^{λh} give zero loss); the claims hold only for the distinguished root in the unit disc, but the statements say 'the global minimizer' (thm:rk_diss even claims uniqueness).

issues.failure_explanation: Under the corollary's satisfiable hypotheses (e.g., e^{λh} = 0.93, δ = 0.7), the condition |e^{λh}| ≤ √(8/9) places the entire level set {|p(z)| = |e^{λh}|} in the open left half-plane, so every root of p(z) = e^{λh} — including the selected minimizer with |λ̂h| ≤ δ — has Re(λ̂) < 0; this is exactly what the paper's own appendix establishes. The claimed Re(λ̂) > 0 is therefore false throughout the hypothesis regime and also contradicts consistency (λ̂ → λ as h → 0 with Re(λ) < 0). Additionally, 'a unique global minimizer' is false: all three roots of the cubic attain the zero loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the Leap-Frog scheme is absolutely stable in the interval $(-1,1)$, the imaginary axis.
Since the roots satisfy $\zeta_1 \zeta_2 = -1$, one of the simple roots always lies outside the unit circle.

issues.failure_explanation: With the strict definition, Leap-Frog's absolute stability region is empty (its characteristic roots satisfy ζ₁ζ₂ = −1, so one root always has modulus ≥ 1), hence ∂R_A = ∅ and the claimed membership is false for Leap-Frog; the later claim that Leap-Frog is 'absolutely stable in (−1,1)' contradicts the same definition. More generally, the learned λ̂h lies on the boundary locus (a characteristic root has modulus exactly 1), but the boundary of R_A need not contain boundary-locus points at which a spurious root lies outside the unit disc, so the one-line proof '|z_n| ≡ 1 ⟹ λ̂h ∈ ∂R_A' is insufficient.

failure_location.quote: it must lie on the boundary of the numerical method's absolute stability region.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: while $\operatorname{Re}(\hat\lambda) $ is always negative under the setting that $a = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed formula is ρ(ζ)/κ(ζ) for ρ(ζ) = ζ²−ζ and κ(ζ) = (−1+8ζ+5ζ²)/12, which are the polynomials of the standard two-step Adams–Moulton method (AM3), not AM2; the repeated-root value (−6±4√3 i)/7 matches AM3's discriminant 84ξ²+144ξ+144 = 0.
